body.heading: Silverline Rail Financial Review: Yard Modernization Program at Westgate Intermodal Yard
paragraphs: Report No. FIN-2026-002
Issued by Silverline Rail, Corporate Finance Department
Published 3 March 2026

body.heading: Executive Summary
paragraphs: This financial review examines the cost position of the Yard Modernization Program at Silverline Rail as at 31 January 2026, twenty months into a thirty-six month schedule. The review was requested by the Audit Committee after the program's monthly cost report first showed a forecast overrun in December 2025.

The review confirms that the program will exceed its approved budget unless scope is reduced, that the process for approving signalling change orders is weak, and that interest capitalised on the works has been overstated. Cost reporting itself is timely and the review found no errors in the reported actual costs.
Four findings and three recommendations are presented. The Chief Financial Officer and the Program Director have accepted all three recommendations.

body.heading: Background
paragraphs: The Westgate Intermodal Yard is the company's principal container transfer facility and handles about 310,000 lifts a year. The Yard Modernization Program is a three-year capital program to rebuild the receiving tracks, install centralised signalling and extend the container loading pad. Civil works are performed by the company's own engineering division.

Signalling design and installation is contracted to Ironbridge Signal Works, a specialist vendor engaged under a fixed-price contract with a change order mechanism. Change orders are raised by the vendor when site conditions or design requirements differ from the tender documents, and are approved by the Program Director.

The review examined the program ledger, all twelve signalling change orders, the interest capitalisation schedule and the monthly cost reports from June 2024 to January 2026, and interviewed the Program Director, the program accountant and the vendor's contract manager.

body.heading: Findings
paragraphs: Finding 1: The Yard Modernization Program is forecast to exceed its approved budget by $4.2 million at completion. Severity: High. The overrun arises mainly from signalling change orders and from a six-month delay to the receiving track rebuild that extended the period of contractor site costs. The forecast assumes no further change orders, which the review considers optimistic.

Finding 2: Change orders from Ironbridge Signal Works were approved without an independent cost estimate in nine of twelve cases. The Program Director approved the change orders on the basis of the vendor's own pricing, and the program has no engineer's estimate against which to test them. The review regards this as a serious control weakness that requires attention before the next reporting period. Three of the nine change orders were priced more than 40 percent above comparable items in the original tender.

Finding 3: Capitalised interest on the Westgate Intermodal Yard works was calculated using an outdated borrowing rate. Severity: Medium. The schedule uses the 6.1 percent rate from the 2023 facility rather than the current weighted rate of 5.2 percent. The effect is an overstatement of capitalised interest of about $190,000 to date.

Finding 4: Monthly program cost reports were issued within five working days of month end in every month reviewed. Severity: Low. Reported actual costs agreed to the general ledger in every month tested. The review notes this as an effective control.

body.heading: Recommendations
paragraphs: Recommendation 1: Rebaseline the Yard Modernization Program budget and present the revised forecast to the Board in April 2026. Priority: High. The rebaseline should include a contingency for further change orders and a decision on whether the container pad extension remains in scope.

Recommendation 2: Require an independent cost estimate for every Ironbridge Signal Works change order above $50,000. Priority: High. The estimate should be prepared by the engineering division or an external estimator before the Program Director approves the change order.
Recommendation 3: Recalculate capitalised interest using the current weighted borrowing rate and adjust the asset ledger. Priority: Medium. The adjustment should be booked before the half-year close.

body.heading: Financial Impact
paragraphs: The forecast cost overrun at completion is $4.2 million, which is 10.9 percent of the approved budget. The approved program budget is $38.5 million, set by the Board in June 2024. Spending to 31 January 2026 was $24.7 million.

Signal change orders approved to date total USD 3,120,000 across twelve change orders. The review could not determine how much of this amount would have been avoided with independent estimates, but the three change orders priced well above tender rates account for $610,000.

body.heading: Appendix
paragraphs: Appendix A: Management response. The Program Director accepts Recommendation 1 and will present the rebaseline at the April 2026 Board meeting. The Program Director accepts Recommendation 2 with immediate effect. The Financial Controller accepts Recommendation 3 and will book the adjustment by 30 June 2026.

Appendix B: Basis of the forecast. The forecast at completion combines actual costs to 31 January 2026 with committed contracts and the engineering division's estimate of remaining civil works. Escalation is included at 3 percent a year.
Appendix C: Distribution. This report is distributed to the Audit Committee, the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief Operating Officer and the Program Director.
